page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and includes 24 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX and AVX-512 instructions. The instance is equipped with 10.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding approximately 2.62 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks place the c5n.xlarge in the lower tiers for most compute and memory tasks. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also rank in the bottom 25%, with Passmark memory scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, the instance demonstrates moderate capabilities in specific workloads, achieving average performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench text processing, and text generation for small language models. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, the c5n.xlarge offers a dedicated compute allocation with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs, combined with its modest memory-to-vCPU ratio, makes it an entry-tier option for network-optimized workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Given its benchmark profile, this instance is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and network-bound utility tasks rather than heavy database operations or intensive multi-threaded compilation.
